lessons.indian-english: te-only lesson (profile te.md §8 'add' / §4.11 / §9): Indian English usages that are normal in India but puzzle listeners abroad (prepone, out of station, good name, passed out, revert, years back, hotel for restaurant), forms wrong in any variety (Myself Ravi, discuss about, I have a doubt for a question) and Telugu calques (Where do you stay?, I'll go and come, native place, simply); English side reused from hi-en's lesson of the same id, localised (Rahul→Ravi, Delhi→Hyderabad), with the Hindi calques replaced by the Telugu ones of te.md §8 (check 3, mc 5, type items 3–4 are new English); placed after smalltalk via profile.json lessonOrder.after; deck 22 «ఇండియన్ ఇంగ్లీష్: ఇక్కడ, విదేశాల్లో»; no ko-en counterpart (replaces the Korean-only konglish of the scaffold; mirrors zh chinglish, hi indian-english)
lessons.question-tags: te-only lesson (profile te.md §8 add, §4.3): question tags matched to the helper verb and the subject (isn't it? only after it is / this is / that is), right? as the safe tag, answering by the facts (No, I'm not), wh-question order with every helper, and statement order in embedded questions (I don't know where he is). The invariant tag is the most frequent Indian English feature in ICE-India (Lange 786; Demszky et al.), Telugu has one tag (కదా) and no inversion, and ko-en has no tag or embedded-question content. New English side (checks and practice written for this course; the practice set meets the article-plural standing rule: order 2/4, type 2/4). Placed after modals (profile.json lessonOrder.after), deck తప్పనిసరి మాటలు 2 (deck 4, the deck of questions).
